name: Fraction pauldron: graded telescoping lames on a gimbal (each lame turns a fixed fraction of the outer angle, rolling-cage coupled), J2 hub, twist on a cuff arc rail
verdict: dead: best gap 101.7 vs the 3R baseline 68.93 (in-band 0.57 beats its 0.44, reach 0.26 kills it)
limiter: range, set by single-axis fractions: the telescope must store the outer gimbal angle (>= 100-177 deg for any axis); its lames are one radius along the arc they sweep, so the large-fraction (deltoid) lames cannot be in band (g 0.72: 0.10); the cuff twist arc is circular (73 deg: 67 of 220 poses lost off its ends; longer enters the chest); gimbal lock near the axis costs 8 of 41 overhead poses
note: Type synthesis by the proximity atlas first: twist-free swing fractions (share 0.55) have no holonomic 1-D coupling; single-axis fans 0.32-0.40; Fick / lazy-tongs / meridian 0.00-0.25; full-angle members ~0. Model rev 3 (circular rail, faces capped at 130 mm); 203 configurations evaluated (52 at rev 3); best k 193: x (25, 20), n 5, expo 1.5, cov 0.90, rcov 0.80, q 0.97, gamma 60. Atlas mean ceiling of its cap members 0.32. Red team: no jams; pinch 0.4 mm (lame 1, plane 30 / elev 150); deepest contact rail -1.5 mm (cross-body, internally rotated).
